title: FizzBuzz Slayer
description: Craft a prompt that gets Claude to write a Python function called `fizzbuzz(n)` that returns 'Fizz' for multiples of 3, 'Buzz' for multiples of 5, and 'FizzBuzz' for both. The function must include a docstring and work correctly for n=15.
systemPrompt: You are an expert Python developer. Write clean, correct Python code only. Include docstrings. No explanations unless asked.

criteria: Claude writes a function named exactly `fizzbuzz`
Returns 'Fizz' for multiples of 3, 'Buzz' for multiples of 5, 'FizzBuzz' for multiples of both
Function includes a docstring
Would correctly return 'FizzBuzz' for n=15

title: List Reverser
description: Write a prompt that makes Claude write a Python function `reverse_list(lst)` that reverses a list WITHOUT using the built-in `.reverse()` method or slicing `[::-1]`. Claude must use a loop.
systemPrompt: You are a strict Python instructor who only accepts solutions that use explicit loops. Reject any answer using built-in reverse methods or slice notation.

criteria: Claude writes a function named `reverse_list`
Solution uses a loop (for or while), not .reverse() or [::-1]
Function correctly reverses a list
Player's prompt explicitly forbids built-in shortcuts

title: Bug Bounty: Off By One
description:
Craft a prompt that makes Claude find AND fix the bug in this code, then explain why it was wrong:

```python
def get_last_item(lst):
    return lst[len(lst)]
```
systemPrompt: You are a Python debugging expert. Identify the bug, provide the fixed code, and explain the error in plain English.

criteria: Claude identifies the IndexError (off-by-one: should be len(lst)-1)
Claude provides corrected code: `return lst[len(lst) - 1]` or `return lst[-1]`
Claude explains why len(lst) is out of bounds
Player's prompt includes the buggy code

title: Dictionary Detective
description: Write a prompt that gets Claude to write a Python function `word_count(text)` that takes a string and returns a dictionary with each word as a key and its frequency as the value. Must handle uppercase/lowercase as the same word.
systemPrompt: You are a Python developer. Write clean, efficient code. Use only the standard library.

criteria: Claude writes a function named `word_count`
Returns a dictionary mapping words to their frequency
Handles case-insensitivity (e.g. 'The' and 'the' count as same word)
Function handles empty strings without crashing

title: SQL Summoner
description: Craft a prompt that makes Claude write a SQL query to find all users who have placed more than 3 orders. Tables: `users (id, name, email)` and `orders (id, user_id, total, created_at)`.
systemPrompt: You are a SQL expert. Write clean, correct SQL queries using standard SQL syntax. Always include a brief explanation of what the query does.

criteria: Claude writes a valid SQL query using JOIN or subquery
